ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Nanomaterials

Nanomaterials: Materials with at least one external dimension between 1 and 100 nm 

Nanoscience is the study of phenomena and synthesis, characteristisation , exploration and exploitation of nanostructured materials 

Nanotechnologies are the design, characterisation, production and application of structures, devices and systems by controlling shape and size at nanometer scale

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Nanomaterials

Classification of Nanomaterials
Zero dimensional nanomaterials (0D) : Materials having all the dimensions within the nanorange where no dimension is allowed to be outside of nanorange. Like quantum dots , nanoclustures eg. fullerene.

One dimensional nanomaterials(1D): Materials having one of their dimensions out of the nanorange eg. nanotubes , nanowires

Two dimensional nanomaterials (2D) : Materials having two of their dimensions out of the nanorange eg. Nanofilms, nanocoatings

Three dimensional nanomaterials (3D): Materials having all the three dimensions out of the nanorange eg. Dispersions of nanoparticles, bundles of nanowires

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):

Nanomaterials

Nanomaterials possess specific properties which maybe significantly different from bulk properties
Reasons 
Large fraction of surface atoms / unit volume:
Properties are dictated by surface atoms rather than bulk atoms
Eg Pt sheet  versus Pt powder

Source:https://nanosense.sri.com/activities/sizematters/introduction/SM_Lesson1Student.pdf

Large surface energy : Surface atoms are held with less force as compared to bulk. Surface activity high .Eg Al

Source slide page 12 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Nanomaterials

Surface Area dependant properties
Many physical and chemical properties of a material depend on its surface properties
 Surface area is enormously increased on moving from bulk to nano scale.
 Nanomaterials have a significant proportion of atoms existing at the surface
Properties like catalytic activity, gas adsorption depend on surface area
     e.g. Bulk gold is catalytically inactive but gold nanoparticles are catalytically very active for selective redox reactions
Surface energy is also high so chemical reactivity is high
     e.g. Aluminium becomes combustible

Source slide page 13 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Nanomaterials

Optical Properties - Increase in Energy gap
Increases in energy gap between the valence band and conduction band
 As size of nanoparticles decreases the energy gap increases and the wavelength of light absorbed moves towards smaller values . This is referred to as ‘blue shift’ 
    eg. colloidal suspensions of gold nanoparticles :
     Gold spheres of > 50 nm  absorb at λ  = 575 nm
     Gold spheres of 10- 20 nm absorb at λ  = 524 nm
     Gold spheres of 2-5 nm absorb at λ = 517 nm

Source::https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colloidal_gold

[00:00:00.388] Hello everyone, welcome back to this course on engineering chemistry. We will continue with module two on nanomaterials and in this class we are going to talk about properties of nanomaterials, surface area dependent properties, electrical properties and optical properties.
[00:00:19.044] Properties of nanomaterials are very different from that of the bulk materials. We find that for bulk material the properties are independent of size whereas when we come to nanomaterials they change with size. For example, if we have a block of gold
[00:00:36.816] Then it is it has a particular colour that is uh called golden colour. Now even if you make it into smaller and smaller size, like for example, the block of gold which was say hundred grams, now we make it into a five gram piece, by breaking it into smaller pieces, we find that.
[00:00:54.384] There is no change in the colour, it still continues to remain in that golden colour. But that is not true when we come to the nanoparticle range. Gold, when we get it into the nanoparticle range, we find that as we decrease the size, the colour of gold also.
[00:01:11.952] So changes. So what does it tell us? That the optical properties are getting altered with the dimension of the particles. So this
[00:01:23.408] Is what happens for all most of the properties of nanomaterials. They change with size. Now, if at all we want to change the bulk material properties, it can be done only if we change the structure and the composition. Whereas in nanomaterials, the material remains the same.
[00:01:41.104] The structure composition remains the same, it's only the size which is changing, and that can alter the properties.
[00:01:49.284] Let us look at the most important property of nanomaterials, the surface area. We know that many physical and chemical properties of a material are going to depend on surface properties, and when we come to nanomaterials, the surface area has enormously increased.
[00:02:07.972] Where in a bulk, let us look at this picture here. We have a bulk material over here, it is being broken down into smaller particles. We know that the surface area has increased so much over here. Now if you make it further smaller, again we find a large increase in nano in the
[00:02:25.808] The surface area. Now if you go to nanometer range, then definitely the surface area is going to be very high. And we know that since in nanomaterials the surface atoms are much more than what the atoms at inside the bulk of the material and therefore
[00:02:45.808] All the properties are mostly dictated by the surface atoms. And since we have such a large surface area, such a large number of surface atoms, therefore the properties which depend on surface area definitely get affected when you take.
[00:03:04.832] the particle when take the material from bulk to nanocyte. So properties like catalytic activity we know that whenever we use a catalyst we prefer to take it in the powder form because we want to increase the surface area and catalytic catalysis is a surface phenomena. So definitely
[00:03:22.480] If we take it in nano range, nano particle range, the catalytic activity is going to increase enormously. Similarly, gaps gas absorption also depends on surface area. For example, bulk gold is found to be catalytically inactive, but gold nanoparticles.
[00:03:40.096] Are found to be catalytically very active for selective redox reactions. Now, another important fact which we discussed.
[00:03:49.508] In the previous class, that the surface energy of these nanoparticles is very high. Why? Because there are a lot of surface atoms which are held much less tightly as compared to the bulk atoms. So therefore, the energy of the surface is going to be very
[00:04:07.280] very high and every system tries to lower its energy so we find that it can do so by uh by uh the reactivity we find that this gets projected in the high chemical reactivity of the nanoparticles so because of this
[00:04:24.848] high surface energy, the chemical reactivity is also very high, and this uh I have quoted before that aluminium, though it is in bulk, it is found to be passive, when it comes in the nanoparticle range, it is found to be combustible.
[00:04:41.604] Let us talk of the next property that is electrical property. For nanoparticles, it is found that electrical conductivity decreases as compared to the bulk material. The
[00:04:53.744] One important reason for that is spatial confinement. We talked about spatial confinement also, and we understood that as we go into the nanoparticle range.
